title: Degree-zero module cohomological descent for an open-cover face total site
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $(W_i\hookrightarrow T)_{i\in I}$ a set-indexed open cover [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-size-convention]. Set $T_n=\coprod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_n)\in I^{n+1}}(W_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap W_{i_n})$. Retain only the injective order maps and their index-dropping morphisms. Form the small Zariski ringed total site [def-sc-zariski-site] with the structure sheaves $\mathcal O_{T_n}$, its ordinary module category $\mathscr M$, and the augmentation $a$ of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. Thus $(a^*G)_n$ is the restriction of $G$ to each tuple intersection. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every $\mathcal O_T$-module sheaf $G$, regarded as a complex in degree zero, the canonical derived adjunction unit is an isomorphism
$$\eta_G:G[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_*(a^*G[0]).$$
Here $Ra_*$ is the ambient right derived augmentation pushforward computed by K-injective resolutions. There is no quasi-coherence hypothesis on $G$, no finiteness condition on the cover, and no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness hypothesis on $T$.

source.place: Tag 0D7F, lemma-augmentation-spectral-sequence-modules, injective alternating-face resolution proof; combined with cohomology.tex Tag 01EQ, lemma-cech-cohomology, and Tag 01EP, lemma-injective-trivial-cech. proof.text: Choose a nonnegative injective resolution $G[0]\to K^\bullet$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_T)$: [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] apply to the small Zariski ringed site. Open restriction is exact and preserves injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives]. Thus $a^*$ and every face pullback are exact: their components are restrictions to tuple intersections, and exactness in the total category is componentwise by [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. Put $J=a^*K$. This resolves $a^*G$, and every $J_p^q$ is injective. Indeed modules on a disjoint union are families of modules on the summands (sections and maps glue uniquely on the disjoint open cover); a lifting problem into such a family is a family of lifting problems into $K^q|_{W_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap W_{i_p}}$. Each has a lift by the cited restriction lemma, and choosing these set-many lifts supplies a lift in the product category.

source.place: Tag 01E1, lemma-cohomology-of-open; disjoint-open gluing and componentwise exactness

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-face-component-injective-total-model] with $F=a^*G$, $J=a^*K$, $\phi=\operatorname{id}_{a^*G}$ and $t=\operatorname{id}_{a^*K}$. All its exactness and componentwise injectivity hypotheses were verified in step 1. Its total complex has
$$C^{p,q}=\prod_{\mathbf i\in I^{p+1}}j_{\mathbf i,*}(K^q|_{W_{\mathbf i}}),\qquad W_{\mathbf i}=\bigcap_{r=0}^pW_{i_r},$$
where $j_{\mathbf i}:W_{\mathbf i}\hookrightarrow T$: on an open $V\subseteq T$, sections of the disjoint union over $V$ are exactly $\prod_{\mathbf i}K^q(V\cap W_{\mathbf i})$. The face transposes are restrictions with the alternating signs. The same cited theorem identifies the morphism represented by the restriction augmentation $b:K^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}(C)$ with the canonical unit $\eta_G$, as a derived morphism, not merely on cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0D7F, lemma-augmentation-spectral-sequence-modules, double-complex proof using lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation-modules and lemma-augmentation-cech-complex-modules. Agent adaptation to injective order maps and componentwise injective resolutions, including augmentation normalization.

proof.text: For every open $V\subseteq T$, the row augmentation $K^q(V)[0]\to C^{\bullet,q}(V)$ is the ordinary Čech restriction augmentation for the open cover $(V\cap W_i)_i$ of the scheme $V$. Its coefficient module $K^q|_V$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives]. Consequently [lem-sc-injective-module-cech-augmentation] makes this row augmentation a quasi-isomorphism. The degree-zero projections here are precisely restrictions, and restriction of scalars at $V$ is along the identity ring map, so the normalization hypotheses of that node hold. Hence $0\to K^q\to C^{0,q}\to C^{1,q}\to\cdots$ is an exact sequence of sheaves: its section sequence is exact on every open, which implies sheaf exactness directly by the local criterion for the image sheaf. The rowwise quasi-isomorphism criterion [lem-sc-first-quadrant-column-augmentation], with the horizontal face degree as its resolution direction, now shows that $b$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its chain-map condition is restriction commuting with $d_K$; its horizontal-kernel condition is $s|_{V\cap W_j\cap W_i}-s|_{V\cap W_i\cap W_j}=0$. Both indices are nonnegative, so each total diagonal is finite even when $I$ is infinite.

proof.text: By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the quasi-isomorphism $b$ becomes invertible under $Q$. Composing with $G[0]\simeq QK$ and the total-model isomorphism of step 2 gives exactly $\eta_G$, so $\eta_G$ is invertible. No assertion about convergence of an unbounded double complex is involved: the object being resolved here is a module in degree zero and both resolution indices are nonnegative.
